description: What would it take to make life beyond Earth possible? Our vision is to turn scientific ideas into an engaging journey that sparks curiosity, encourages critical thinking and inspires the next generation to look beyond Earth. We believe the future of exploration begins with imagination, curiosity and the courage to ask, “What if?”

details:
KESSLER is an interactive space-exploration and outpost-management game designed for children aged 7–12. Players choose to establish an outpost on the Moon or Mars and take on the challenge of managing the resources and systems needed to sustain life beyond Earth.

The game introduces players to real space-engineering challenges through resource management and mission decisions. Players manage supplies such as water, oxygen, electricity and food while learning about radiation protection, environmental conditions and communication delays. These systems introduce engineering trade-offs: using resources for one operation can affect what is available for another. The mission experience is designed to help players understand that space exploration requires careful planning, prioritisation and problem-solving.

KESSLER also places a strong emphasis on learning and discovery. Its Space Encyclopedia connects players to scientific research and space-agency educational resources. Explanatory animations and simple, step-by-step explanations make complex concepts easier for young learners. Pop-up questions appear during gameplay to encourage players to apply what they have learned. Correct answers earn prizes, stars and bonus points recorded in a Learning Log, while incorrect answers are followed by friendly explanations so that mistakes become learning opportunities.

Our aim is to make space science engaging and accessible while helping children understand the decisions behind human exploration. We want players to leave with more than space facts: we want them to understand why resources are limited, why engineering choices involve compromises and how scientists and engineers solve problems.

We developed KESSLER using the Instaplay game-building platform, with AI-assisted support during development and project writing. The experience combines interactive gameplay, educational content, research links, animations and a reward system. Our team considered the target age group, scientific accuracy, understandable explanations, meaningful resource trade-offs, engagement, accessibility and the importance of distinguishing real scientific information from simulated game values.

KESSLER's creative approach is to bring together outpost management, guided science learning, research discovery and positive reinforcement in one experience. We hope to inspire young players to become curious about space exploration, science and engineering.
KESSLER – Project Details

What does our project do and how does it work?

KESSLER is an interactive space-exploration and outpost-management game designed for children aged 7–12. It puts players in the role of space mission planners, challenging them to understand what it takes to sustain human life beyond Earth.

Players can:

  • Choose their destination: Begin their journey by selecting the Moon or Mars.
  • Manage an outpost: Balance essential resources such as water, oxygen, electricity and food.
  • Face real space challenges: Explore radiation protection, environmental conditions, food production and communication delays.
  • Make important decisions: Experience engineering trade-offs where using resources for one operation can affect another.
  • Discover how space systems work: Learn about the processes and technology involved in supporting human life beyond Earth.

What benefits does KESSLER offer?

KESSLER transforms learning from simply reading information into an interactive experience where children can explore, experiment and apply their knowledge.

Our game features:

  • A Space Encyclopedia: A collection of educational information and links to scientific research and space-agency resources, allowing players to explore beyond the game.
  • Step-by-step explanatory animations: Visual explanations that break down complicated scientific processes into simple, child-friendly lessons.
  • Easy-to-understand explanations: A range of explanations designed to make space science accessible to young learners.
  • Interactive pop-up questions: Knowledge questions appear throughout gameplay to encourage critical thinking and test players' understanding.
  • Rewards and encouragement: Correct answers earn prizes, encouraging stars and bonus points.
  • A personal Learning Log: Players can see their earned stars and bonus points and keep track of their learning achievements.
  • Learning from mistakes: Incorrect answers are followed by fun, helpful explanations so players understand the correct answer instead of feeling discouraged.

What is the intended impact of our project?

Our mission is to turn children's curiosity about space into a genuine interest in science, technology and engineering.

We want to:

  • Introduce younger audiences to the challenges of human exploration beyond Earth.
  • Make complex scientific and engineering concepts easier to understand.
  • Encourage problem-solving, strategic thinking and decision-making.
  • Show children why resources are limited and why engineering decisions involve compromises.
  • Create a positive learning environment where mistakes are opportunities to improve.
  • Inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers and space explorers.

We want children to finish playing KESSLER with more than just space facts. We want them to understand the thinking, planning and innovation behind humanity's future in space.

What tools, software and technologies did we use?

Our team developed KESSLER using:

  • Instaplay: Our primary game-building and development platform, used to create the interactive game experience.
  • ChatGPT: An AI-assisted tool used for brainstorming, developing ideas, refining educational explanations, preparing development instructions and improving project content.
  • NASA and Canadian Space Agency resources: Scientific and educational materials linked through our in-game research centre.

KESSLER is designed as a browser-based experience, allowing players to access the game online. No specialised hardware was required. The underlying programming languages used by the platform were not independently identified by our team.

How is our project creative and innovative?

KESSLER brings together space exploration, engineering challenges, scientific discovery and interactive education in one experience.

What makes our approach special is that learning is woven into every part of the adventure:

  • Children don't just read about space missions; they take on the responsibility of managing an outpost.
  • They don't just memorise scientific facts; they discover concepts through animations and apply their understanding through decisions.
  • They don't simply answer questions; they receive explanations, encouragement and rewards.
  • They aren't limited to the information presented in the game; they can explore our Space Encyclopedia and follow links to further scientific research.
  • They don't have to feel discouraged by mistakes; every incorrect answer becomes another opportunity to learn.

By combining mission management with guided learning, interactive questions, rewards and independent research, KESSLER aims to make space education both meaningful and exciting.

What factors did our team consider during development?

We wanted to create an experience that was scientifically meaningful while remaining enjoyable and understandable for children. Our team considered:

  • Target audience: Designing explanations, animations and challenges suitable for children aged 7–12.
  • Scientific accuracy: Connecting educational content to genuine scientific research and identifying the sources of information.
  • Meaningful gameplay: Making resource management and engineering decisions an important part of the experience.
  • Accessibility: Presenting complicated scientific ideas in simple language and visual explanations.
  • Engagement: Keeping players interested through exploration, interactive questions, mission challenges and rewards.
  • Positive learning: Encouraging experimentation and making mistakes a natural part of the learning process.
  • Educational value: Ensuring that players understand the science behind their decisions, rather than simply completing challenges.
  • Authenticity: Distinguishing real scientific research from simulated gameplay values.

OUR VISION

KESSLER isn't just about exploring another planet. It's about understanding what it would take to call it home.

We hope to inspire children to look beyond the stars, ask bigger questions, challenge themselves and discover that the future of space exploration begins with curiosity.
